display.purpose: The brand in the head-bar and each project page's h1 title. Same 0.875rem size; 800 weight, 0.22em tracking, uppercase.

headline.purpose: Section headings and write-up panel h2s over a 2px ink rule. 800 weight, 0.2em tracking, uppercase; metric values run 800 at 0.04em.

title.purpose: Index project links, bold readout lines, data-table headers, the active TOC link. 700 weight.

body.purpose: Prose. Measures: write-up prose ~72ch, status lede 72ch, subtitles 64ch, summaries 68ch, taglines 52ch. 400 weight, tabular figures.

label.purpose: Nav links, back link, chips, dates, meta-bar entries, metric labels. 400 weight, 0.08em tracking, uppercase, secondary ink.

motion.name: register
motion.value: opacity 0 to 1, 0.24s cubic-bezier(0.16, 0.84, 0.3, 1), per-block delay var(--d) = block order * 110ms
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: homepage floorplan blocks register one-by-one once on load. Guarded by prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: state-fade
motion.purpose: Hover/press opacity and background transitions (block dimming to 30%, pressed block 70%, index row 5%/9% ink tints). No movement or scaling anywhere.

motion.name: smooth-anchor
motion.purpose: Anchor scrolling on the homepage; suppressed via sessionStorage flag when arriving from a project page so cross-page anchors jump instantly.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: Homepage floorplan/index grid collapses to one column with the index first (order: -1); floorplan panel caps at 560px.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Nav becomes a 2x2 ruled grid; section heads stack; timeline dates fold above bodies; title-grid stacks; metrics strip folds to 2x2; fig-grid stacks.

breakpoints.name: toc
breakpoints.purpose: Minimum width at which the fixed right-rail page TOC appears on project pages.

components.name: Nav Link
components.description: Uppercase tracked label link; secondary ink resting, ink + 1px bottom border on hover. External links carry a literal ↗. Shared on every page.
components.css: .ds-head-nav { display: flex; gap: 22px; font-family: 'Martian Mono', 'Courier New', monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.7; } .ds-head-nav a { text-decoration: none; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink-2, #555c64); border-bottom: 1px solid transparent; } .ds-head-nav a:hover { color: var(--ink, #22262a); border-bottom-color: var(--ink, #22262a); } .ds-head-nav a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink, #22262a); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Prose Link
components.description: Ink text underlined in the hairline color; underline darkens to ink on hover.
components.css: .ds-link { font-family: 'Martian Mono', 'Courier New', monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--ink, #22262a); text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-color: var(--rule, #b9beb2); text-underline-offset: 4px; } .ds-link:hover { text-decoration-color: var(--ink, #22262a); } .ds-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink, #22262a); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Block Swatch
components.description: 18px square block-color fill with a 2px solid ink border; dashed border when the project is in progress.
components.css: .ds-swatch { display: inline-block; width: 18px; height: 18px; background: var(--bin, #2f9e44); border: 2px solid var(--ink, #22262a); } .ds-swatch-live { border-style: dashed; }

components.name: Index Row
components.description: The crawlable index row: swatch + 700-weight link, uppercase date, tagline, bare metric line, actions. Fully clickable; active is a 5% ink tint, pressed 9%.
components.html:
• R500JUN 2025 – PRESENT

    A 32-bit pipelined processor on the Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA.

    57 MHz · 1.23 CPI · 96.5% branch prediction
components.css: .ds-legend-row { list-style: none; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 30px 1fr; gap: 4px 16px; padding: 16px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule, #b9beb2); cursor: pointer; font-family: 'Martian Mono', 'Courier New', monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.7; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; transition: background-color 0.18s ease-out; } .ds-legend-row:hover { background: rgba(34, 38, 42, 0.05); } .ds-legend-row:active { background: rgba(34, 38, 42, 0.09); } .ds-lr-swatch { width: 18px; height: 18px; margin-top: 3px; background: #2f9e44; border: 2px solid var(--ink, #22262a); } .ds-lr-top { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: baseline; gap: 8px 16px; flex-wrap: wrap; } .ds-lr-link { font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: var(--ink, #22262a); text-decoration: none; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule, #b9beb2); } .ds-lr-link:hover { border-bottom-color: var(--ink, #22262a); } .ds-lr-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink, #22262a); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-lr-date { color: var(--ink-2, #555c64); letter-spacing: 0.04em; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-lr-tagline { color: var(--ink-2, #555c64); margin: 4px 0 0; max-width: 52ch; } .ds-lr-metric { margin: 6px 0 0; letter-spacing: 0.03em; color: var(--ink, #22262a); }

components.name: Section Head
components.description: Section heading over a 2px ink rule with a right-aligned secondary-ink note. Shared chrome; write-up panel h2s use the same ruled treatment.
components.html:
Projects

Click a block or a row to read the full write-up
components.css: .ds-section-head { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: baseline; gap: 16px; border-bottom: 2px solid var(--ink, #22262a); padding-bottom: 8px; font-family: 'Martian Mono', 'Courier New', monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.7; } .ds-section-head h2 { margin: 0; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.2em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink, #22262a); } .ds-sh-note { color: var(--ink-2, #555c64); letter-spacing: 0.03em; }

components.name: Data Table
components.description: Ruled tabular readout: hairline borders, 2px ink rule under uppercase headers, right-aligned numerals, bottom caption linking the source raster.
components.css: .ds-data-table { border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid var(--rule, #b9beb2); font-family: 'Martian Mono', 'Courier New', monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.7; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--ink, #22262a); } .ds-data-table caption { caption-side: bottom; text-align: left; color: var(--ink-2, #555c64); padding: 10px 2px 0; letter-spacing: 0.03em; } .ds-data-table th { text-align: left; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; border-bottom: 2px solid var(--ink, #22262a); } .ds-data-table th, .ds-data-table td { padding: 8px 16px; } .ds-data-table td { border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule, #b9beb2); } .ds-data-table td + td, .ds-data-table th + th { border-left: 1px solid var(--rule, #b9beb2); text-align: right; } .ds-data-table caption a { color: var(--ink, #22262a); text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-color: var(--rule, #b9beb2); text-underline-offset: 4px; } .ds-data-table caption a:hover { text-decoration-color: var(--ink, #22262a); }

components.css: .ds-plate { margin: 0; border: 1px solid var(--rule, #b9beb2); background: var(--paper-deep, #e3e6dd); padding: 12px; font-family: 'Martian Mono', 'Courier New', monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.7; } .ds-plate-img { height: 120px; background: repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, rgba(34,38,42,0.16) 0 1px, transparent 1px 7px); border: 1px solid var(--rule, #b9beb2); } .ds-plate figcaption { color: var(--ink-2, #555c64); margin-top: 10px; letter-spacing: 0.03em; }

components.name: Timeline Node
components.description: 11px square timeline node on a hairline axis: solid ink = done, paper-filled dashed = current.
components.css: .ds-trav { display: inline-flex; gap: 18px; } .ds-trav-node { width: 11px; height: 11px; background: var(--ink, #22262a); border: 2px solid var(--ink, #22262a); } .ds-trav-node-live { background: var(--paper, #edefe8); border-style: dashed; }

narrative.overview:
The site presents William Park's work as a placed-and-routed die: each project is a labeled IP block on a pad-ringed chip floorplan, carrying a real measured result, the blocks tiling the die edge-to-edge with no gaps. The world is a light engineering document — plot-paper ground, graphite ink, hairline rules — with color reserved almost entirely for the saturated block fills that identify projects. It explicitly refuses the dark neon card-grid developer portfolio.

The world governs the entire site. The homepage is its Persuade surface (the drawn die, the index, the timeline); the project pages are its Read surfaces (ruled write-ups with figure plates and data tables). One drawing engine (docs/js/plan-lib.js) draws the homepage die. The legacy dark stylesheet (css/style.css) has been deleted; nothing outside this world exists anywhere on the site.

The silicon world stays implicit in form: the drawing does the talking, and the copy never names the metaphor. There are no report-form labels anywhere — no "wafer", "process", "lot", "device", "bin", no MEAS: prefixes. Measured numbers stand bare in running copy; on Read surfaces they may sit in ruled readouts (a metrics strip, a data table) whose plain uppercase headers are instrument labeling, not metaphor dressing. Structure comes from ruled lines and grids, not boxes or shadows; hierarchy comes from weight, tracking, ink value, and spacing, never from type size. Status is expressed in mark form (solid outline = shipped, dashed = in progress) rather than in prose badges.

The site is hand-editable static HTML/CSS/JS deployed from docs/ via GitHub Pages with no build step — a hard, permanent constraint. New projects append via js/projects.js (plus the noscript list). Every raster carries embedded provenance (impeccable:prompt metadata); video posters are ffmpeg-extracted first frames of the site owner's own demo videos.
keyCharacteristics: Light plot-paper ground with graphite ink; color only in block fills
The silicon metaphor is drawn, never written: no report-form vocabulary in copy
One monospaced type size everywhere; hierarchy by weight/tracking/ink/spacing
Hairline rules and 2px section rules structure the page; no cards, no shadows
Status is drawn, not written: solid vs. dashed marks
Measured numbers are real and tabular; bare in copy, ruled into readouts on Read surfaces
One drawing engine: the homepage die is drawn by PlanLib from the projects data

rules.name: The Two-Ink Rule
rules.body: All text is one of two inks: #22262a for content, #555c64 for labels and metadata. Emphasis is a change of ink or weight, never a change of color.

rules.name: The Block-Fill Rule
rules.body: Saturated color appears only as a project's identity fill (floorplan blocks and index swatches). Interface chrome — links, nav, chips, rules, focus — is ink on paper.

rules.name: The One Size Rule
rules.body: All HTML text is 0.875rem. Hierarchy is weight (400 / 700 / 800), tracking, uppercase, ink value, and spacing — never font size.

rules.name: The Bare Number Rule
rules.body: Copy never names the silicon metaphor and never dresses data in report vocabulary — no "wafer", "process", "lot", "device", "bin", no MEAS:-style prefixes. In running copy and index rows a measured result stands bare ("57 MHz · 1.23 CPI · 96.5% branch prediction"). Ruled readouts on Read surfaces — the metrics strip and data tables — carry plain uppercase labels and column headers: native instrument labeling of a table, not metaphor vocabulary in prose.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: No shadows, no lifted surfaces, no gradients. State is shown by opacity, ink shifts, and border changes on the same plane.

rules.name: The Mark-Form Rule
rules.body: In-progress status is always drawn as a dashed stroke on the element's existing outline, never as a colored badge or icon.

rules.name: The One Plan Rule
rules.body: There is one floorplan. Every die on the site — the homepage floorplan — is tiled by the PlanLib core-and-periphery placement from the PROJECTS data, so block positions match everywhere. Never hand-place or redraw the plan.

dos: Do keep all HTML text at 0.875rem Martian Mono; build hierarchy with weight (400/700/800), 0.08–0.22em tracking, uppercase, and the two inks.
Do structure new surfaces with rules and grids: 2px ink for section structure, 1px #b9beb2 hairlines for dividers; recessed material sits on Plot Paper Deep inside a hairline frame.
Do draw in-progress status as a dashed stroke on the element's existing outline, and shipped as solid.
Do show real measured numbers (tabular figures): bare in copy and index rows; in a ruled metrics strip or data table on Read surfaces. A metric field is only ever a genuine measurement.
Do render every die through PlanLib from PROJECTS so block placement matches site-wide; keep drawn SVGs aria-hidden enhancements over real links, with focus sync and noscript fallbacks.
Do keep files hand-editable plain HTML/CSS/JS — no build step, ever; new projects append via js/projects.js plus the noscript list.
Do use only the owner's real artifacts: rasters carry embedded provenance, video posters are extracted first frames of the actual demos.
donts: Don't introduce a second type size, a second typeface, or a dark background — this world is the refusal of the dark neon card portfolio, and the legacy dark stylesheet is deleted, not dormant.
Don't use report-form vocabulary in copy: no "wafer", "process", "lot", "device", "bin", no MEAS:-style prefixes in prose. The silicon world lives in the drawing, not the words.
Don't use box-shadows, gradients, sheen, rounded corners (radius is 0), or card containers; grouping is rules and whitespace and the die is drawn flat.
Don't put block colors on text, links, buttons, or chrome; they exist only as project identity fills.
Don't invent metrics, and don't replace the mark-form status language with colored badges or icons.
Don't paste screenshots of tabular data; transcribe them into a .data-table and link the source raster from the caption.
